findings.claim: WP-SCP-020 §8 (line 188) bus-factor-1 risk row was not updated at 020K delivery to remove stale scp-break-glass team references, creating a contradiction with 020K AC(a) and D-031(a) which both state no team is created.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-020 §8 line 188 reads: 'The `scp-break-glass` team (020K) and `SCP-CODEOWNERS` set both initially name James only' and escalation step '(a) add them to `scp-break-glass` team'. But WP-SCP-020 §4 020K (line 114) says explicitly '(a) no `scp-break-glass` team created' and D-031 DECISIONS.md line 43 says 'NO `scp-break-glass` GitHub team is created — GitHub teams are not available on user namespaces'. D-031 escalation path correctly reads 'add them to `CODEOWNERS`' with no team reference, establishing a direct contradiction between the two authoritative documents. CODEOWNERS comment (line 6–8) correctly omits any team reference, confirming the implementation is correct while the plan §8 record is stale.
findings.impact: §8 is the authoritative risk record cited by D-031 body ('§8 bus-factor-1 risk row remains LIVE'), the CODEOWNERS comment ('see WP-SCP-020 §8 + STATUS.md'), and the STATUS.md scheduled-follow-ups entry source column. A future operator or agent executing the §8 escalation procedure on second-maintainer onboarding will attempt step '(a) add them to `scp-break-glass` team' — which cannot succeed because the team does not exist on a personal user namespace. The correct single-step procedure is 'add them to CODEOWNERS'. The stale reference also misleads agents that parse §8 to assess whether a break-glass team is active: the text implies it exists and names James, when in fact it was never created.
findings.mitigation: Amend WP-SCP-020 §8 line 188 in two places: (1) replace 'The `scp-break-glass` team (020K) and `SCP-CODEOWNERS` set both initially name James only' with 'The `SCP-CODEOWNERS` set initially names @jrnb2024 only (no `scp-break-glass` team — not available on personal user namespaces, per 020K U-k resolution 2026-04-21)'; (2) replace escalation step '(a) add them to `scp-break-glass` team, (b) add them to `SCP-CODEOWNERS`' with '(a) add them to `CODEOWNERS`'. Both edits are in-scope for 020K since §8 is the risk record this slice is responsible for marking as LIVE. The fix does not alter any AC; it removes false state from an authoritative document.

findings.claim: WP-SCP-020 §8 bus-factor-1 risk row lacks an explicit LIVE/CLOSED status marker; multiple downstream artifacts (D-031, STATUS.md, auto-memory) reference it as 'LIVE' but the plan prose uses 'Accepted as operational exposure' without a machine-readable badge.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-020 §8 line 188 text begins with the risk description directly, with no `[LIVE]` or `[CLOSED]` badge. D-031 DECISIONS.md (line 43) says 'remains LIVE'. STATUS.md scheduled-follow-ups table entry (line 64) cites the source as the plan §8. D-031 escalation path says 'amend §8 risk row to CLOSED' — implying the current state is LIVE — but the risk row itself does not carry this marker, making the inverse assertion (it is now LIVE) inferential rather than explicit.
findings.impact: Trivial for human readers who can infer LIVE from the absence of a CLOSED marker. Potentially confusing for automated agents or future tooling that scan §8 for risk-row status badges. The ambiguity grows if more risk rows are added to §8 in later slices.
findings.mitigation: Add `**[LIVE]**` before 'Today SCP has a single operator' in the §8 bus-factor-1 risk row. This is a one-word inline change and can be bundled with the MAJ-001 fix in the same amending commit.
